cells.tense: What you held through a hard change is steady now, and it can stand a fair give and take.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: With whoever shares in what you're growing, hand over what you'd usually keep and accept what's offered back at full size, so both directions stay open.
cells.core:
What came through the clearing is more settled than you notice. The young thing — a routine, a person, a project you stayed with — has roots, and you've stopped bracing for it to be torn up again. That steadiness is the win, and from here it can survive being shared.

Put it into a fair trade.** With someone who's part of this, pass over what you would normally keep — a turn, an hour, the easier half of the work — and take something back at its true size. It can be small. The exchange runs both ways and doesn't need a ledger. What you're protecting gets stronger by moving, not by sitting in your hands.
cells.sheetLine: What you held through the change is steady — let it move.
cells.verb: holding what a hard change finally won
cells.place: where something young is being tended without being rushed

cells.tense: A share you will want to make is being readied for ahead of time, and the tending has started bracing.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: Next time you reach to guide what you care for, wait a day and hold every way it could go without choosing any, just watching what that's like.
cells.core:
In what you tend, the need to have it ready keeps arriving early. You can see four versions of how it should grow and you want the right one locked before anyone else can see the doubt. From where you sit that reads as care; from the other side it can feel like the growing thing has already been decided for.

Hold the cloud.** When the next push to steer or prepare arrives, name it as a moment, not a verdict. Let yourself be pulled toward what might happen without acting on it yet — one day of no choosing. You don't have to know whether it's safe or right; you only have to leave the space open long enough for the actual shape to show. Connection here isn't the same as steering, and you can feel both without picking one.
cells.sheetLine: The bracing comes before the share. Let the share come first.

cells.tense: After the hard change settled, a care that used to run openly has stayed at the door it walked through.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Choose a direction you actually want for something growing near you, and the next time something pulls you off it, take the same heading again.
cells.core:
Something finished, and you came out of it with steadier ground. But the attention that used to move toward what's young has gotten cautious. You see a person doing well and say nothing. You have a way you want something to develop and don't set the condition. The care is there — it shows in how closely you watch — but it stays back from what it watches, waiting on a permission you already have.

Defend one direction.** Choose a single thing you want to grow and, the next time something pulls you off it, take the same heading again. No speech, no explanation; one refusal of the pull. The point isn't to prove you care. It's to move the attention back from watching into the doing it's for.
cells.sheetLine: The ground is steady. The attention stays back from what it watches.

cells.tense: The conditions you set for what grows are already doing their work, authored by a hand you haven't signed.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Settle one condition for what you're tending, act it the same day, and carry it without a case made for it.
cells.core:
The shape of what grows around you keeps coming from you — the timing, the allowance, the small rule that makes a space safe — and your own account has you as the one who simply stays out of the way. Whoever is growing here can feel the frame. So can the person who shares it. The author is at the desk. The byline is missing.

Decide one thing and carry it.** Choose a single condition for what you're tending this week — a time, a limit, a yes — settle it in one motion, and act the same day. No announcement, no argument for it. You'll find out something you half-know: the structure holds because you set it, and it holds better when you've owned the setting than when it runs as if it happened to no one.
cells.sheetLine: You set the conditions. Sign the work that's holding.

attempts.check: The record does not license the claim that the person has actually stopped tending; Too Little says only that the capacity shows up past-anchored, so the reader could rightly object that care still happens daily in some form. The ask (defend one chosen direction against the next push) is still useful if that read is wrong, because choosing a real thing and holding it costs nothing and teaches whether anything has been dropped. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line that points to a specific door they walked past; I have kept the core to the present shape of the slowing and the missing pick, so it can be refused and still leave something usable.
